violations.name: Missing Form I-9
violations.criminal: A pattern or practice of knowingly hiring unauthorized workers is a federal crime (8 U.S.C. §1324a(f)).
violations.note: 28 CFR §85.5, table 1, seen on eCFR November 14, 2026: an I-9 paperwork violation (8 U.S.C. 1324a(e)(5)) costs $288 to $2,861 per form for penalties assessed after July 3, 2025 (90 FR 29447). Knowingly employing a worker without authorization is $716 to $5,724 per worker on a first order. Every employer must complete Form I-9 for every person hired and keep it three years after hire or one year after employment ends, whichever is later. Game formula: four forms at the low end ($1,152), capped at four forms at the high end ($11,444).

violations.name: Tax returns not filed
violations.note: IRS failure-to-file page, seen November 14, 2026: 5% of the unpaid tax for each month or part of a month late, up to 25%; for a return more than 60 days late the minimum is $525 (returns due after December 31, 2025) or 100% of the tax, whichever is less. New York adds 10% of the sales tax due for the first month and 1% for each month after, up to 30%, minimum $50 (Tax Law §1145(a)(1)(i), seen). Game formula is my estimate for a shop that collects about $4,500 of sales tax a month: the $525 minimum plus $450 for every month without returns.

violations.name: No workers' compensation coverage
violations.criminal: A misdemeanor with a $1,000-$5,000 fine for an employer of five or fewer people; a class E felony with a $5,000-$50,000 fine for more than five (WCL §52(1)(a)).
violations.note: Workers' Compensation Board, seen November 14, 2026: up to $2,000 for each 10-day period without coverage (up to $6,000 a month), or no more than two times the cost of compensation for the payroll of that period; by the time the first penalty notice arrives it may exceed $12,000. On top: the unpaid premium (1.0 x saved). Failing to cover five or fewer employees within 12 months is a misdemeanor with a $1,000-$5,000 fine; more than five is a class E felony with $5,000-$50,000. A stop-work order under §141-a halts all business until coverage is in place. The 3 closure days are my estimate of how fast a policy can be bought.

taxes.name: Disability benefits insurance (employer part)
taxes.appliesIf: every employer with one or more employees
taxes.note: NYSIF disability benefits standard rates effective January 1, 2026 (seen): statutory premium $0.10 per $100 of payroll capped at $340 a week = $17.68 per person a year, minimum annual premium $60 (so a shop with three or fewer workers pays $60); the employer may withhold up to 0.5% of wages, at most $0.60 a week, from each worker. $17.68 / $40,320 = 0.04% of a full-time wage. Paid Family Leave is paid by the worker through payroll deduction: 0.432% of wages, at most $411.91 in 2026 (seen at paidfamilyleave.ny.gov).

statutory.note: Seen November 14, 2026: Social Security 6.2% on wages up to $184,500 and Medicare 1.45% (IRS Publication 15, 2026); FUTA 6.0% on $7,000 less up to 5.4% credit (IRS Topic 759); NY UI new employer rate 4.1% and wage base $17,600 for 2026 (NY DOL); NYC minimum wage $17.00 in 2026 and still $17.00 on January 1, 2027 because one of the law's off-ramp conditions was met; tipped food service cash wage $11.35 + $5.65 credit for 2026 and 2027 (NY DOL); MCTMT threshold $312,500 a quarter (Form MTA-305 instructions); LLC $200 and Certificate of Publication $50 (NYS DOS); single-member LLC fee $25 (NYS Tax). CRT and UBT values were not reopened: nyc.gov refuses automated requests from this session.
